specification.outcome: Normal conversation can create an ordinary Backlog task or replace an unclaimed Backlog task specification without requiring a campaign or starting work.

scenarios.name: atomically create an ordinary task
given: create-task is a closed valid request and the verified board is writable
when: the host durably journals and publishes it
then: one task-created-from-request event atomically projects the complete initial task
the task has no campaign provenance and no readiness or work effect
a published or reconciled receipt identifies the exact authority event and board head

scenarios.name: amend only a backlog specification
given: specify-task has an exact canonical TaskId, a parsed replacement, and the target is unclaimed Backlog
when: the host publishes task-specified-from-request against the observed task-version digest
then: only specification and specification digest change
all other task state is preserved
an unchanged replacement returns unchanged without creating an event

scenarios.name: reject concurrent same-task ABA changes
given: an amendment binds the digest of all authority event IDs affecting the task through the observed head
when: another writer changes the task and later restores the same specification and lifecycle values
then: the task-version digest still differs
publication returns TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT
the stale amendment never overwrites intervening authority

scenarios.name: retry unrelated head advancement safely
given: the operation journal binds stable operation and event identifiers, canonical request digest, expected task version when applicable, and observed head
when: the remote gains events for unrelated tasks
then: the host verifies the new head and revalidates all bound identities and target state
the unchanged event JSON is committed under the new parent and the new commit is signed
same-task or identity changes conflict

scenarios.name: recover every consequential boundary
given: the journal is in intent-written, commit-prepared, push-attempted, observed-published, receipt-recorded, or terminal-denied
then: intent-written revalidates before preparing; commit-prepared observes parent/head before push; push-attempted observes remote before retry; observed-published reconstructs receipt; terminal states do not replay
an exact published operation reconciles only from the matching local journal
uncertain or mismatched authority returns conflict and never duplicates an event

scenarios.name: apply closed parsing and denial precedence
given: a create-task or specify-task request contains malformed or unauthorized facts
when: the host parses once and evaluates facts until the first result
then: create precedence is TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_VALUE_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TIBER_TASK_ID_COLLISION, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT

amend precedence is TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_ID_INVALID, TIBER_SPECIFICATION_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TIBER_TASK_NOT_FOUND, TIBER_TASK_LIFECYCLE_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_SPECIFICATION_UNCHANGED success, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT
denied requests publish no task authority

scenarios.name: route independently of campaigns
given: the user asks to create a ticket or edit an unclaimed Backlog specification
then: it requests create-task or specify-task rather than campaign-goal or begin-task
campaign state is neither required nor changed
no readiness review or claim begins

acceptanceCriteria: create-task has exactly kind:create-task,title,description. No optional specification is accepted; specification is a separate specify-task operation. Title is a trimmed nonempty string of at most 200 UTF-16 code units and description is a string of at most 10000; null, undefined, wrong types, unknown keys, and duplicate raw JSON keys are invalid.

specify-task has exactly kind:specify-task,taskId,specification. TaskSpecification has exactly outcome,scenarios,acceptanceCriteria,exclusions,dependencies,testMappings,architectureImplications; scenarios have exactly name,given,when,then. Existing nonempty and length bounds apply. Unknown, missing, null, undefined, partial, duplicate raw JSON keys, and wrong types are invalid.

All accepted strings reject unpaired UTF-16 surrogates. Canonical UTF-8 is the WHATWG TextEncoder encoding of host-constructed fixed-key-order JSON.stringify output. Arrays preserve order and null or omitted fields never enter canonical values.

TaskId is lowercase canonical hyphenated UUID version 1 through 5 with RFC variant 8,9,a,b; whitespace, uppercase, braces, compact, nil, ambiguous references, and unsupported versions return TIBER_TASK_ID_INVALID.

task-created-from-request schema is schemaVersion,eventId,kind,occurredAt,operationId,requestDigest,task. task contains id,title,description. Initial projection is state Backlog; blockStatus unblocked; specification, specificationDigest, claim, finalReviewProgress, completionRelease, delivery, ci, openedReview, reviewReceipt, campaignProvenance all Option none; preservedIncrements empty; it has no Ready rank or priority and appears in deterministic task creation order.

task-specified-from-request schema is schemaVersion,eventId,kind,occurredAt,operationId,requestDigest,taskId,expectedTaskVersionDigest,specificationDigest,specification. Reconciliation compares operationId, requestDigest, eventId, taskId, expected version, replacement digest, and canonical specification.

Canonical create request digest input is fixed-order kind,title,description. Amend input is kind,taskId,specification with fixed TaskSpecification/scenario key order. requestDigest is lowercase SHA-256 of canonical UTF-8 prefixed sha256:. taskVersionDigest is lowercase SHA-256 of canonical ordered event IDs affecting the task through the observed head, also prefixed sha256:.

Before journaling, create generates operation/task/event UUID triples and amend generates operation/event pairs. All IDs are checked against complete verified history and active journals; if any generated ID collides the whole tuple is regenerated, up to three tuples. Exhaustion returns TIBER_TASK_ID_COLLISION. After journaling identifiers never change; any nonexact reuse conflicts.

First publication requires operation and generated IDs absent. Uncertain-publication recovery with a matching local push-attempted or observed-published journal reconciles an exact existing event. A fresh request or mismatched journal never treats an existing operation ID as success.

The private journal uses a repository-scoped exclusive cross-process lock. Every state is written to a same-directory temporary file, file-fsynced, atomically renamed, and directory-fsynced before the next effect. Lock acquisition failure is TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT. Denials after intent become terminal-denied audit records; pre-intent parse or authority denials create no journal.

A prepared Git commit and signature are retained local recovery/audit effects, not published task authority. Events are canonical JSON inside a Git tree; the containing Git commit is signed over tree, parent, author, committer, and message. On unrelated head advancement event JSON and IDs stay fixed while parent, commit ID, and signature are replaced after revalidation. Unauthorized or conflicting prepared records become terminal-denied and are never pushed.

Create published or reconciled receipt is {code:TIBER_TASK_CREATED,disposition,taskId,eventId:{kind:some},boardHead,specificationDigest:{kind:none}}. Amend published or reconciled is {code:TIBER_TASK_SPECIFIED,disposition,taskId,eventId:{kind:some},boardHead,specificationDigest:{kind:some}}. Unchanged is {code:TIBER_TASK_SPECIFICATION_UNCHANGED,disposition:unchanged,taskId,eventId:{kind:none},boardHead,specificationDigest:{kind:some}}. boardHead is the exact verified head establishing that result.

Denials are {code,operation:create-task|specify-task,taskId Option,retryability,requiredRecoveryEvidence}; only exact requested task ID is public safe context. No journal paths, signer material, commit bytes, or capabilities are disclosed.
Ordinary create and amend never promote, prioritize, review, claim, start, or alter campaign state.
exclusions: Changing title or description after creation
Creating and specifying atomically in one request

src/core/tasks/readiness.ts exact specification parser and canonical digest
src/core/tasks/task-board.ts new event projection, task-version calculation, initial state, and lifecycle
src/adapters/tasks/git-task-remote.ts verified history, signing, observation, and fast-forward publication

specification.architectureImplications: Add closed create-task and specify-task requests, task-created-from-request and task-specified-from-request events, purpose-specific operation and task-version digests, and a durable repository-scoped operation journal. The host owns exact parsing, canonicalization, bounded identifiers, locking, lifecycle and ABA checks, signing after revalidation, uncertain-outcome observation, and receipts; inference grants no authority and cannot start work.
